TESLA / SPARKS / CASE STUDY 08

Manufacturing Equipment & Vision Inspection

Support production equipment through mechanical design, vision inspection, PLC logic, and robotics.

01 Problem02 Requirements03 Concepts04 Engineering Analysis05 Design06 Build / Test07 Results08 What I Learned
01

Problem

During my equipment engineering internship in Sparks, I supported production equipment through mechanical design, PLC logic, robotics tools, and vision sensing.

My work included CAD, TIA Portal, ROBOGUIDE, and a Keyence IV2 vision-sensor application. The goal was to connect hardware changes with predictable equipment behavior.

02

Requirements

RequirementEngineering definition
IntegrationConnect mechanical design, controls, and sensing.
OperationConsider production use and operator interaction.
AutomationUse PLC and robotics tools for equipment support.
InspectionEvaluate the vision setup in its actual lighting conditions.
VerificationCheck equipment behavior after a change.
03

Concepts

ITERATION / 01

Begin with the equipment

Understand the mechanical arrangement, sensing, and operating sequence before changing the logic.

ITERATION / 02

Treat sensing as a system

Evaluate the vision sensor together with lighting and setup, rather than treating the camera as an isolated component.

04

Engineering Analysis

The work involved TIA Portal ladder logic, CAD, and ROBOGUIDE, with an IV2 vision-sensor application that included lighting changes.

A reported trial achieved approximately 93% vision accuracy. The figure is specific to that trial and is not presented as a production-wide inspection guarantee.

05

Design

Equipment work included a suction-cup and actuator design for robotic handling, PLC mass checks at three-second intervals, and a vision-sensor application.

Mechanical layout, sensing, lighting, and the operating sequence were considered together during equipment support.

06

Build / Test

Equipment-level evaluation included vision-sensor and lighting checks. A pulse-tester board replacement was followed by a 24-hour pass.

These results describe separate equipment-support tasks completed during the 2023 internship.

07

Results

The experience built a practical connection between mechanical equipment and the controls that operate it, with verification tied to the particular task.

~93%vision accuracy in reported trial
3 sPLC mass-check interval
24 hpulse-tester pass
08

What I Learned

Reliable automation depends on the interfaces. Lighting affects sensing, mechanical behavior affects sequencing, and operator needs affect how a control system should be presented.
